scope: Independent source, protocol schema, transport, lifecycle, saved-data admission and statistical wiring review. Original selected-native four-engine-v3 sources were read as historical references only. No historical timing result was reused, recomputed or overwritten.

findings.problem: The immutable quiet-grant contract binds source manifest, CPU, allowed process labels and one invocation's budget, but not the specific attempt directory. prepare.py can therefore create multiple timing run IDs using the same grant bytes, and each run.py invocation independently receives a new 900-second budget. The private attempt directory prevents overwriting one attempt, but does not prevent a grant from being applied to another new attempt. Root explicitly requires unique-attempt positive one-shot timing admission.
findings.required_change: Require the root grant to bind the absolute attempt_directory and identify its positive one-shot authority. Check the binding in preparation, before process launch and in saved admission. Retain all existing CPU/source/budget/SMT/quiet checks. The independently reviewed generated-protocol SHA must remain an explicit execution input. Avoid a circular protocol-SHA/grant-SHA binding if the protocol itself embeds the grant SHA.

findings.problem: The runner writes stdout_sha256 and stderr_sha256 after owned cleanup, but analyze.py only rehashes protected/tool/input files, raw.jsonl and executables. None of the twelve retained per-process stdout/stderr logs is rehashed during saved-data admission. A changed or missing log can therefore coexist with a clean analyzer admission despite the terminal receipt claiming exact saved log identities.
findings.required_change: Require exact six-label inventories in receipt stdout_sha256 and stderr_sha256, and rehash every corresponding label.stdout.log and label.stderr.log before statistics. Treat any missing, extra or changed retained log as a global provenance failure. Keep raw event accounting and all mathematical gates unchanged.
